solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle getting parked outside, one's learned

indicators.note: outside says the word for parked sits around the vehicle

parts.note: to have parked oneself is to have sat
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A learned person turns up in a vehicle and has it parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's learned' reads as 'one is learned', i.e. a learned one.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a scholar, someone of great learning.

clue.text: Part of spring roll, chilli powder, syrup and semolina last of all served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read from bottom to top
last of all asks for the final letter of each of the foodstuffs listed

explanation.surface: A recipe: a spring roll with chilli powder, syrup and semolina, served.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters L, I, R, P, A of roll, chilli, powder, syrup and semolina are read upwards; 'and' only joins the list.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in the middle of the northern spring season.

clue.text: National data to preserve, measure taken to conceal it

indicators.note: the measure is taken round the data and preserve, hiding them inside

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres
gen is informal British for information
to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: Instructions for archiving national records: keep the data, take steps to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this is a citizen of the South American republic.

clue.text: Raised bar in a number of games — of this?

definitions.text: Raised bar in a number of games — of this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are written from bottom to top
in puts the bar inside the number of games

parts.note: a set is a group of games in this sport
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A query about a sport whose net is raised and which is played in sets of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns SINNET upwards. Read whole, the clue describes the game itself: a raised net, games grouped in sets.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the racket sport played over a raised net in sets of games.

clue.text: Area where papers returned, complete

indicators.note: returned means the word for papers is read backwards

parts.note: ID, identity documents, are papers
strict can mean absolute or complete, as in strict secrecy

explanation.surface: A place where newspapers have come back in full.
explanation.walkthrough: Strict = complete is a stretch the blogger also queried; Collins lists it.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or locality, an area.

clue.text: Man, old crossword setter eating last of pud — that fills a gap?

parts.note: a man is a playing piece in draughts, so a draught
ex means former or old

indicators.note: eating means the setter takes the letter inside

parts.note: a cluer is one who writes clues, a crossword setter

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word pud

explanation.surface: An elderly setter of crosswords tucking into pudding, which fills a gap in his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a draughts piece, called a draught in Britain; the definition plays on filling a gap under a door, not in a stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught excluder is a long padded strip laid along a door's bottom to block cold air entering the gap.

clue.text: Triallist is female with record on track

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
an EP is an extended-play record
to dog is to track or follow closely

explanation.surface: An athlete in trials who is a woman holding a record on the running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triallist' is a competitor in sheepdog trials, contests where dogs herd sheep, not a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Working dogs compete in herding contests called trials, so such a dog is a triallist.

clue.text: Career's ending with brief farewell for broadcaster

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the word career
brief means the farewell is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, a farewell

explanation.surface: A career ends with a short goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a receiver set, and the word also covers the broadcasting medium itself.

clue.text: Frenchman turned over after gendarme confiscates an appliance

indicators.note: after puts the reversed name following the policeman piece
confiscates means the policeman takes the word an inside

parts.note: a gendarme is a French policeman, a cop

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means the name is written upside down, letters reversed

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A French policeman seizes a device from a Frenchman after he is overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is a kitchen gadget, a small appliance for opening cans.

clue.text: Outfit in dress, highway robbery

indicators.note: in puts the outfit inside the dressing

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Robbery on the road committed by someone in fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigandage is banditry, the plundering of travellers by bandits.

clue.text: Racket sport's ultimate force

parts.note: a racket is a din, a loud noise

indicators.note: ultimate picks the last letter of the word sport

explanation.surface: In racket sports, the decisive thing is power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' wants to be a tennis racket; it is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dint means power or effort, surviving in the idiom by dint of.

clue.text: Damned batting!

definitions.meaning: a mild British expletive adjective, meaning bloody or confounded
batting an eyelid is opening and shutting the eyes rapidly

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a batsman's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a mild curse and the action of eyelids flickering.

clue.text: Spur is sharp

definitions.meaning: to spur is to urge or prod into action
sharp means on time, punctual, as in six o'clock sharp

explanation.surface: A spur has a sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to urge on; as an adjective it means punctual or immediate.

clue.text: Queen fled with yours truly

parts.note: fled means ran away
yours truly is the speaker, me, so I

explanation.surface: A queen ran away, taking the writer with her.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is an Indian queen or a rajah's wife.

clue.text: Diversion in the early hours sent me off round Ukrainian capital

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the hours after midnight

indicators.note: capital picks the first letter, the head, of Ukrainian
off means the letters of sent me are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sent away to the Ukrainian capital in the small hours, by way of a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes MSEMENT from SENT ME, which goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is entertainment, something that amuses.

clue.text: Last of meat, dog eating it — that's grand!

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word meat
eating means the dog takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a hound is a dog
it is crossword slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A dog chomping the last of the meat, which is just great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an exclamation of approval; it is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand, especially a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Lead — or sharpened flint?

definitions.meaning: to lead an attack or campaign from the front
a pointed flint fixed to the top of a shaft, a weapon tip

explanation.surface: A choice between a metal and a stone for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the leading force of a campaign and the pointed tip of a thrown weapon.

clue.text: Those looking to grab knickers primarily — when this?

definitions.text: Those looking to grab knickers primarily — when this?

indicators.note: to grab means the onlookers take the letter inside

parts.note: starers are people who look fixedly

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of knickers

explanation.surface: People gawping at underwear being snatched, wondering when someone will be left naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks when onlookers would grab at knickers: when one is naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for completely naked.

clue.text: Further demand to drink extra bubbly

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: bubbly means the letters of extra fizz into a new order

explanation.surface: A request for more, to drink some extra champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' wants to be champagne; it is the anagram signal on 'extra', giving ERTAX.
explanation.definitionFit: A supertax is an additional levy on high incomes, a further charge demanded.

clue.text: King dressed in silver once, light colour

indicators.note: dressed in means the king is clothed by the coin, placed inside it

parts.note: the ecu was an old French coin, often of silver
R, rex, is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king once dressed in silver, a pale shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Tenor's possible autobiography incomplete, a victim of hubris

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Enrico Caruso, the great tenor, might title his memoir I, Caruso

explanation.surface: A singer's memoir, left unfinished, about a man brought low by pride.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this boy flew too near the sun on wax wings, the classic tale of overweening pride.

clue.text: Cool tune

definitions.meaning: to cool is to moderate or soften
to tune an instrument by adjusting its intervals

explanation.surface: Praise for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to moderate and to tune an instrument to a tuning system.

clue.text: In particular, a king of old

indicators.note: In means the letter a goes inside the word for particular

parts.note: prim means fussy or particular

explanation.surface: A specific monarch from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In particular' reads as a phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Homer's Iliad, a monarch of antiquity.

clue.text: Slash the time taken to tie your shoes?

definitions.meaning: to slash is to cut or gash

definitions.text: the time taken to tie your shoes?
definitions.meaning: the speed of doing up laces

explanation.surface: Cut the time it takes to do up shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into LACE RATE, a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or cut flesh, to slash it.

clue.text: Short letters from Peter Sellers

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Brief correspondence from the comic actor Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and curt, short in speech.

clue.text: Shop steward's back before priest

indicators.note: back picks the final letter of the word steward

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A shop steward comes back ahead of a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Real v Atletico Madrid, say, about to go wrong? That's juicy!

indicators.note: about means the derby goes around the words for going wrong

parts.note: a match between local rivals is a derby; in Spanish style, el derby
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A football fan's verdict that the Madrid derby, gone awry, is gripping stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: A derby is a match between rivals from the same city; the Spanish press call it 'el derbi'.
explanation.definitionFit: This small dark fruit is notably juicy, used for wine and cordial.

clue.text: Spray moister with a spray can

indicators.note: spray means scatter the letters of moister and a

explanation.surface: An instruction to dampen something using an aerosol.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine mist, much like an aerosol spray can.

clue.text: Shelter on ground that's wet

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the shelter after the ground

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground
a den is a shelter or lair

explanation.surface: A shelter built on soggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, thoroughly wet.
